seg_p0038_s0001: But at last, when countless peoples had been enlightened by their preaching, Torquatus of Acci, Tisephon of Vergium, Secundus of Abula, Indaletius of Urci, Caecilius of Eliberri, Esicius of Carseca, and Eufrasius of Eliturgi rested, namely on the Ides of May.”
seg_p0038_s0002: And so indeed in the Roman Martyrology (which Baronius confirms was once published under Jerome's name, together with a likewise supposititious letter of the same Jerome to Chromatius and Heliodorus), as also in the martyrologies of Bede, Usuard, Notker, and Ado, at the Ides of May, we read that “these men were ordained bishops at Rome by the holy apostles, and were sent into Spain to preach the word of God; and when they had evangelized in various cities, and had brought countless multitudes under the faith of Christ,” they at last rested in the said places of Spain. In the old martyrology of the Roman Church, which Ado prefixed to his own, nothing else is said of them than that “they were ordained at Rome by the apostles.” But in the British martyrology, which Ricemarchus, son of Sulgenus bishop of Menevia, saw to be transcribed, they are not even named. Yet in the catalogue of the apostles, which is there appended to the letter to Chromatius and Heliodorus, it is recorded of James: “He preached to Spain and to the western regions, and under Herod he fell, slain by the sword.” Orderic Vitalis, the monk of Ouche, adds, in the second book of his Ecclesiastical History, that seven of his disciples carried his body into Spain, “and, being received by the king of Galicia, first preached the faith and religion to the Iberians.” Whether Vincent somewhere found “Hiberni” (the Irish) written in place of “Hiberi” (the Iberians), I leave for others to conjecture; certainly it is not far from the truth that, through some error of this kind, the said disciples of James were transferred to Ireland.
